hints.content:
The number lines show that the ratio of $\maroonD{\text{kilograms}}$ to $\blueE{\text{percentage}}$ is $\maroonD{60}:\blueE{100\%}$.

We are looking for ratios that are equivalent to $\maroonD{60}:\blueE{100\%}$.

$\blueE{100}\div\blueE{20} = \purpleE5$

So. we can find the mass for $\blueE{20\%}$ by dividing both parts of the ratio by $\purpleE{5}$.

[[☃ image 1]]

So $\blueE{20\%}$ of $\maroonD{60}$ is $\maroonD{12}$.

options.alt: A double number line with 3 unequally spaced tick marks. The line labeled Mass, kilograms, reads from left to right: 0, 12, 60. The line labeled Percentage, reads from left to right: 0 percent, 20 percent, 100 percent. An arrow from the pair 60 to 100 percent to the pair 12 to 20 percent is labeled divided by 5.

hints.content:
Now we can find the mass for $\blueE{40\%}$ by multiplying both parts of the new ratio by $\purpleE{2}$.

[[☃ image 1]]

So $\blueE{40\%}$ of $\maroonD{60}$ is $\maroonD{24}$.

options.alt: A double number line with 4 unequally spaced tick marks. The line labeled Mass, kilograms, reads from left to right: 0, 12, 24, 60. The line labeled Percentage, reads from left to right: 0 percent, 20 percent, 40 percent, 100 percent. An arrow from the pair 12 to 20 percent to the pair 24 to 40 percent is labeled times 2.

hints.content:
###Completed table

Mass ($\text{kg}$) | Percentage
-:|-:
$60$ | $100\%$ of $60\,\text{kg}$
$12$ | $20\%$ of $60\,\text{kg}$
$24$ | $40\%$ of $60\,\text{kg}$
